assessment.nobel_worthiness: A genuine game-changer: ionizable lipid nanoparticles made systemic delivery of siRNA and mRNA practical, and this has had enormous real-world consequences, from patisiran to the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines. The chemistry (pKa tuning of ionizable lipids, rapid-mixing self-assembly, PEG-lipid control) is simple in concept and decisive in effect.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) carry the foundational lipid-nanoparticle and ionizable-lipid work; Anderson and Langer contributed combinatorial lipid discovery and broader delivery platforms. Three names must be chosen from six, so Cullis, MacLachlan and Anderson are my proposal, with Hope/Madden and Langer excluded by the three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale and independently confirmed; timing is ripe, particularly after the 2023 Medicine prize recognised the mRNA side but not the delivery chemistry.
uncertainties: Credit among Cullis group members, Anderson and Langer is contested and the three-laureate limit forces hard exclusions.
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize could be read as double recognition of the mRNA vaccine story.
I am relying on my own recollection of priority for ionizable lipid design, not on verified records.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Car-Parrinello method (1985) made first-principles molecular dynamics routine by unifying electronic structure and ionic motion; it opened ab initio simulation of liquids, interfaces, reactions and condensed matter. It is the kind of theory that connects quantitatively to experiment and has shaped computational chemistry for four decades.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is unusually clean: the two credited names are the sole originators and fit a two-person prize naturally. Parrinello also appears under metadynamics and machine-learned potentials, but this is his clearest and most foundational contribution.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of independent adoption and extension (CPMD, Born-Oppenheimer variants); recognition is arguably overdue, and the field has absorbed it into standard practice.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to recognise Parrinello for this or for later methods (metadynamics, MLIPs) is open.
The 2013 prize on multiscale models and the 2024 computational protein prize may make the committee wary of another purely theoretical award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert one base into another without double-strand cleavage by fusing deaminases to a Cas9 nickase; this is a chemically elegant and conceptually new way to edit genomes. Consequences are already real, with clinical trials and treated patients, and the approach is widely used in research.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the concept and development; Komor (cytosine base editors) and Gaudelli (adenine base editors, which required evolving a deaminase acting on DNA) made decisive first-author contributions. Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) have a parallel and near-simultaneous claim, which complicates priority and is why I leave them out only with some unease.
assessment.maturity: Roughly a decade of validation with independent replication and first clinical results; timely rather than premature, though long-term clinical outcomes remain to be seen.
uncertainties: Priority dispute with Kondo and Nishida for cytosine base editing.
Liu also appears in the prime editing and DNA-encoded library candidates, and I would not reward him across several entries.
Whether the committee sees this as Chemistry rather than Medicine, given the 2020 CRISPR precedent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C-N coupling made aryl amines, which are ubiquitous in pharmaceuticals and materials, accessible in a simple and general manner. The ligand design work turned an obscure tin-amide reaction into a broadly usable method; it is a clear game-changer for synthesis and was already widely used in industry.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic amination with amines directly and drove its generality; Kosugi and Migita's earlier tin-amide chemistry is the precursor but not the general method. Two names give a clean prize configuration.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly mature, with 30 years of independent adoption and routine industrial use; the Suzuki, Heck and Negishi prize of 2010 sets a clear precedent.
uncertainties: Kosugi's priority as precursor may be debated by colleagues in organic chemistry.
Hartwig also appears in the C-H functionalization candidate, so allocation across entries needs care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate non-canonical amino acids at defined sites using orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs; it has given protein chemists a new toolkit with many applications in biology and therapeutics. It is new in kind and has produced real consequences.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang provided the first demonstration in living cells (2001) and the general approach; Chin extended it to eukaryotes, multiple codons and engineered ribosomes. Mehl and Yokoyama have valid but narrower claims, so three names are defensible but not uncontroversial.
assessment.maturity: Well established and reproduced widely in academic labs, with growing therapeutic use (for example site-specific antibody conjugates); timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Relative weight of Schultz, Wang and Chin, and the position of Yokoyama.
Whether the impact is mainly through biology applications rather than chemistry in itself.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass-spectrometry-based proteomics, including shotgun identification, quantitative labelling and targeted and data-independent acquisition, turned protein analysis into a systematic, genome-scale measurement. The impact on biochemistry and medicine is immense, and it builds directly on the earlier ionisation methods that were already recognised in 2002.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the leading names for the conceptual and methodological breakthroughs (high-resolution workflows, SRM/SWATH, MudPIT/SEQUEST); Gygi, Hunt and Heck contributed substantively, so allocation is a real problem with the three-person cap.
assessment.maturity: Mature and with extensive independent confirmation; a discipline now routinely used in clinical research.
uncertainties: The credit is spread across many strong groups, so any three-person selection is open to dispute.
The Orbitrap (separate entry) and ionisation methods overlap, and the committee may favour an instrument-focused prize instead.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity through PROTACs and molecular glue degraders reframes drug discovery as event-driven pharmacology and opens undruggable targets. The concept is simple and powerful, and it unified mechanisms of thalidomide-like compounds with rational design.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies initiated PROTACs (2001); Ciulli made a structure-based VHL ligand and a rational design step. The molecular glue side (Handa, Ito, Gray, Kim, Sakamoto) is a distinct line that may need separate recognition; I keep the proposal to the PROTAC concept.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing with many clinical candidates, but approved drugs are still few; there is a risk that recognition now is slightly early.
uncertainties: Clinical benefit is not yet firmly established across the class.
It is unclear whether PROTACs and molecular glues are a single discovery for prize purposes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's work on covalent targeting of the KRAS G12C mutant and his chemical genetics of kinases (analogue-sensitive alleles) showed that a protein long regarded as undruggable could be hit selectively, which led to approved drugs. The consequences are tangible and the chemistry is direct.
assessment.attribution: Only one name is credited, so attribution is simple, though KRAS drug development involved a large industrial effort (Amgen, Mirati) beyond the initial discovery. A one-person prize would be unusual but permissible.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation (approved KRAS G12C inhibitors) supports timing, but second-generation inhibitors and resistance mechanisms are still evolving.
uncertainties: Whether a one-person award is wise given the many contributors in the later drug development.
The kinase chemical genetics and KRAS covalent drugging are two parts of a compound candidate that may differ in maturity.
